choices.text: An ice cube shrinks into a puddle on a warm counter.

choices.text: Salt seems to vanish when it is stirred into water.

questions.workedSolution: In 2 L of water, salicylic acid: 2 × 2.4 g = 4.8 g; new powder: 2 × 3.3 g = 6.6 g. Difference: 6.6 g − 4.8 g = 1.8 g. (Or: the gap is 3.3 g − 2.4 g = 0.9 g per liter, and 2 L × 0.9 g per liter = 1.8 g.)
questions.explanation: Solubility tells how much can dissolve in a given amount of liquid at a given temperature, so twice as much water can hold twice as much. Per liter the new powder dissolves 0.9 g more than salicylic acid, so in 2 L the gap doubles to 1.8 g. A solubility number only means something when you know how much liquid it is for.

choices.text: A solubility test
choices.rationale: Correct: A dissolves well while B barely dissolves, a large difference that is easy to detect.

choices.text: A boiling point test
